incident: development-database file fingerprint changed during an invalid launcher attempt

what_happened.attempt: the first launcher execution used DATABASE_PATH (the pytest-runner isolation contract) instead of DATABASE_URL (the established launcher isolation contract)
what_happened.effect: run.bat [5/7] and [6/7] plus the smoke-stack API startup resolved to the development database (data/writing_feedback.db)
what_happened.launcher_result_still: PASS, exit 0 (health/docs/streamlit 200/200/200) - functional pass, but with the wrong database isolation

root_cause: operator environment error: the launcher contract in this repository's established verification history sets DATABASE_URL (used in the DP0-B launcher run and prior stages), while DATABASE_PATH is the isolated pytest-runner contract; the wrong variable was supplied

logical_integrity_verification.method: read-only sqlite3 inspection of the current file

result.essays_note: 28 essays matches the documented v0.9.6-C-era development state (Submission #28); no audit submission ever touched this database
result.system_versions: all 14 expected rows present with the constant version values; only the recorded_at timestamp changed (07:04:53 UTC) - the standard API-startup version-metadata refresh

logical_integrity_verification.conclusion: zero logical change: no rows added/removed/altered beyond the routine system_versions timestamp refresh; schema, migrations, configuration, and all user data intact

resolution.corrected_launcher_run: executed exactly once with DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///C:/tmp/v096dp0/v1-launcher.db; PASS exit 0; output confirmed the isolated database path
resolution.fingerprint_stability: verified unchanged after the corrected run (F78A6CEA...)
resolution.closure_claim: the development database was not modified by any valid DP0-V1 verification layer; the fingerprint change occurred only in the documented invalid-protocol attempt and is byte-level only with proven logical integrity

lessons_for_report: the final report and documentation disclose the before/after fingerprints and this incident explicitly rather than claiming byte-identical fingerprints
